stem:
A term infant is apnoeic at 90 seconds after birth. The neonatal registrar has begun face-mask ventilation, but the chest is not moving and the heart rate remains 80/min. There is no obvious airway obstruction.

What should the registrar do next?

options.label: A
options.text: Start chest compressions at a 3:1 ratio with the ventilation
options.explanation: Compressions start when the heart rate stays below 60/min despite effective ventilation; at 80/min without chest rise, ventilation is not yet effective.

options.label: B
options.text: Intubate now, before any adjustment of the mask technique
options.explanation: An advanced airway is a later corrective step; simple mask and head corrections come first.

options.label: C
options.text: Increase inspired oxygen to 100% and continue the same ventilation
options.explanation: More oxygen does not help when no gas is entering the lungs; the chest is not moving.

options.label: D
options.text: Give intravenous adrenaline through an umbilical venous line
options.explanation: Adrenaline is for a heart rate below 60/min despite effective ventilation and compressions.

options.label: E
options.text: Reapply the mask for a good seal and reposition the head
options.explanation: No chest movement means ventilation is ineffective; correcting the mask seal and head position are the first corrective steps before escalation.

context: If mask ventilation produces no chest movement, correct mask and airway technique before escalating resuscitation.
